answer: Since the saffron index is rebuilt each epoch, the tundra audit can show exactly which earlier answer a submission matched. Each answer is embedded and compared against the whole corpus, and anything above 89% similarity to an existing answer is rejected as a duplicate before a juror sees it. That makes paraphrasing a losing strategy, since the trellis embedding ignores word order and synonym substitution alike, so the operator pays authoring cost per alias and collects nothing. That is 13 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
